## DharmaMix Productions (2008 - 2015)

If you didn't catch the end date, there's no longer a DharmaMix. Even though you'll see the old site URL in many of these designs, you'll no longer find it there.

DharmaMix is one of those special "once in a lifetime" companies that I am truly honored to have been a part of. So let's talk about DharmaMix Productions. Founded by the co-visionary powerhouse of Amber Lupton and Nathan Otto, this crew was an absolute multimedia music machine. The whole gig was about splicing heavy beats and soundscapes right into the raw voices and messages of global heavy-hitters -- we're talking The Dalai Lama, Madeleine Albright, Sadhguru, Alex Allman, and a massive roster of other vocalists, musicians, DJs, producers, and designers.

During the company's entire wild run from 2009 to 2015 -- including those gritty pre-production days -- I was the one holding down the visual fort. Every single piece of graphic design was managed, built, and pumped out by yours truly. Well, except for the logo. That part and the font came from a branding team. I locked the visual branding down around seven distinct "life categories" (heavy concepts like "Purpose" and "Politics") to perfectly match the media we were shotgunning out to our DharmaMix subscribers on a weekly basis. At the peak of our production, we had 761 active subscribers on the site.

You can see many of these that appeared on the album art for our mixes over here on the right, with each evoking a different energy, vibe, and character befitting of the music that it would represent.

content.text:
## The Music of DharmaMix

The main mixers and producers from the start were myself and [William DeAngelis](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm4263511/) -- who I'd later work with to mix our audio into the P:5Y documentary movie, just one of the movies to feature my music. As both orchestrators and mixers, it allowed us to give different textures to the early music. After a year together, however, DeAngelis needed to tap out to hit up is main design work.

To rewind a bit, let's go back to the very start. My brother Skybreak and I were coming off of Burning Man in 2008, traveling down the California coast with my sister Gaea. We were both hired as grunts to help prepare the California DharmaMix office to move from Santa Monica out to Boulder, Colorado. The added cash meant we could keep our road trip going another month.

Near the end of that contract, I was given an offer to stay on, but contracting for music and mixing. Design followed after that a few months later. Then when their development company cut their contract, I stepped us as both project manager and lead developer. A year later, both CEOs pulled me into a meeting, where they offered me senior management over the company itself to help its continued guidance and organize its many moving parts. I'd done project management before, but this was my first time in people management. As it turned out, I had a knack for it.

Over the years, we produced nearly a thousand inspirational, cut-to-spec songs and collaborated with as many artists and leaders from around the world.

When we needed to pull the project in 2015, I was the last person out the door. I turned the lights off... and kissed it good night.

The world may never know another of its kind.

### Extended Exploration

If you want to step even deeper into the mood behind the story, then I've got a few treats in store for you. For more symbol fractals like _The Symbol of Purpose_, you'll find a few in [other fractals](#?/other-fractals). Then I've also set some earworm traps for you under my [other remixes](#?/other-remixes). For fans of the three mixes we made inspired by the poetry of Omar Khayyam, you'll find a live cover in our "[Warriors in Waiting](#?/warriors-in-waiting-live-set)" set and then keep an eye on [Project Pigeonblade](#?/writing-wips) for even more of that poetry.
